findings.item: review-2 finding 1 (Inspector ownership and RLS proof)
findings.evidence: The Inspector row now names all five existing e2e specs: rait-case-commands, rait-jw01-admissibility, rait-worklist-corrective, rait-worklist-production and policy-routes .e2e.spec.ts. All five exist under backend/app/tests/e2e. It names both shared fixtures, rait-case-command.fixture.ts and rait-jw01-admissibility.fixture.ts, which exist under backend/app/tests/shared. It names the new rait-p402-scope.e2e.spec.ts. It places the RLS tests for the new tables in that Inspector-owned file and requires real role_app_backend request tenant context. It names pnpm verify:rls-ddl, which exists in the root package.json, as an additional gate. Line 129 matches this. The fixtures are now owned, so the 'unowned required path' stop cannot fire because of them.

The Engineer compatibility row says 'Colocated specs are Inspector-owned only; Engineer does not edit tests.' The 'and their colocated specs' grant has been removed. Lines 64-68 assign the colocated specs of the four archive/audit additions 'only by Inspector under apps/rait/web/src/app/'. This agrees with line 58 and with the rule at line 41 that each discipline owns its files.

findings.item: Frontend spec scope is worded two different ways
findings.evidence: Line 58 says the Inspector owns 'named frontend specs', but it does not name any. Line 62 says 'colocated specs'. Two existing wiring specs touch the listed consumers but are not 1:1 colocated with a listed file: data/api/case-admissibility.wiring.spec.ts with data/facades/case-admissibility.wiring.spec.ts, and features/caso/pages/triage.wiring.spec.ts. As written, it is unclear whether either role owns them. Suggested fix: change line 58 to say 'colocated *.spec.ts and *.wiring.spec.ts of the compatibility files listed below'. This does not block approval.

findings.item: Fixture wording is narrower than intended
findings.evidence: The fixtures are limited to 'extend only without deleting fixture coverage'. The stated intent was edit or extend while keeping coverage. 'Extend only' could be read as forbidding edits to existing fixture code. Such edits may be needed when the generated CASE/WORKLIST DTOs or the DDL34/35 tables add required fields. Suggested wording: 'edit/extend without deleting or weakening existing fixture coverage'. This does not block approval.
